claims.claim_text: The indexed Albert Robinso Guay is the Private Albert R. Guay who served as an Area B assistant company clerk after studying personnel management at American University.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive surname and first name, middle-name initial, enlisted status, and direct Area B connection align across the index and official history.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence, but the index's truncated-looking Robinso form is preserved and is not silently expanded into a middle name.
claims.temporal_assessment: American University study is documented before fall 1942 Area B service; the intervening military pathway is unresolved.
claims.match_notes: Box 298 should be reviewed to establish the exact name form, enlistment chronology, and immediate predecessor assignment.

claims.claim_text: Before his Area B service, Guay studied personnel management at American University.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS describes Private Albert R. Guay as a recent American University graduate with a personnel-management major.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official Area B account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS student affiliation, not an employer and not proven to be the immediate predecessor status.
claims.match_notes: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Arden W. Dow is the Washington State ROTC graduate and Fort Lewis Military Police lieutenant ordered to OSS Area B.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name, middle initial, commissioned career, Washington State background, Fort Lewis service, and Area B assignment align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon full name and multiple official biographical identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences Washington State, a reserve commission, 1941 Fort Lewis service, and 1942 Area B orders.
claims.match_notes: The later lieutenant-colonel index rank is consistent with the earlier lieutenant grade in the recruitment account.

claims.claim_text: Dow's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Army Military Police service at Fort Lewis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS places Dow under Blogg at Fort Lewis in 1941 and says military orders sent him to Area B after March 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same detailed official account.
claims.match_notes: This military assignment is not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Before Army service, Dow attended Washington State and completed ROTC.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies the institution and ROTC route to a reserve commission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official biography.
claims.match_notes: Washington State is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Frank A. Gleason is the Penn State chemical engineer and Army Corps of Engineers officer obtained for COI Area B.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and middle initial, commissioned rank, engineering specialty, Army branch, and Area B assignment align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on multiple specific official identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences Penn State and ROTC, April 1942 active duty, and Parkin's COI recruitment.
claims.match_notes: Box 276 remains unreviewed; no civilian employer is inferred from his engineering education.

claims.claim_text: Gleason's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was active duty in the Army Corps of Engineers.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he entered active duty in April 1942 before Parkin obtained his assignment to COI and Area B.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same detailed official biography.
claims.match_notes: The Corps of Engineers is not counted as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Before active Army duty, Gleason studied chemical engineering and participated in ROTC at Penn State.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS supplies the university, field, and ROTC pathway before April 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official biography.
claims.match_notes: Penn State is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Joseph Collart is the Army Captain Joseph H. Collart, a Washington State alumnus and Area B instructor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name and direct OSS Area B context align; the official history adds middle initial, nickname, officer grade, and university association.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon exact name and multiple Area B-specific identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: Washington State predates Area B service, but the immediate pre-OSS assignment and exact commissioning chronology remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The index rank field is blank, so the Captain classification comes from NPS and should be checked against Box 135.

claims.claim_text: Before OSS service, Collart was a student athlete at Washington State.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Area B history identifies Collart with the Washington State alumni and athletic group.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official Area B account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation; the immediate pre-OSS pathway is not established.
claims.match_notes: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Rex Applegate is the Army Military Police lieutenant recruited into OSS training work and later known as Lieutenant Colonel Rex Applegate.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name, Military Police assignment, Fort Lewis connection, Donovan recruitment, and OSS instructional work align across two official histories.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon name and several independent, role-specific official identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: University study preceded his 1940 commission; Military Police and Counter Intelligence Corps training preceded the 1942 Area B role.
claims.match_notes: The NPS Oregon State athletic reference and Army-history University of Oregon graduation are preserved as separate claims rather than silently conflated.

claims.claim_text: Applegate's immediate documented pre-OSS affiliation was Army Military Police service, including the 209th Military Police Company.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS connects his Fort Lewis Military Police service directly to Area B, while the Army history names the 209th company and January 1942 Counter Intelligence Corps course.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence across two official institutional histories.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military pathway; the exact administrative transfer date is not supplied.
claims.match_notes: The military assignment is not a civilian-employer claim.

claims.claim_text: Applegate graduated from the University of Oregon in 1940 before receiving his Army commission.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army history states the institution, year, and sequence into military service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same exact-name and military-career account.
claims.match_notes: The university is not presented as an employer.

claims.claim_text: NPS reports that Applegate played football for Oregon State, but the exact nature and dates of that institutional association remain uncertain.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NPS history supplies the football association; a separate Army history documents his 1940 graduation from the University of Oregon.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence that both sources concern the indexed Rex Applegate.
claims.temporal_assessment: Pre-OSS athletic association with uncertain dates and sequence; not evidence of employment or a degree.
claims.match_notes: The site must display this as qualified evidence and keep the two Oregon institutions distinct.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact Frank A. Gleason name, NARA Captain rank, Penn State chemical-engineering and ROTC background, Army Corps of Engineers duty, and COI Area B assignment align.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 276 and Army records for exact commissioning, April 1942 active-duty, and COI transfer dates and for any civilian employment before active service.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The uncommon exact Rex Applegate name, Army Military Police role, Fort Lewis connection, Donovan recruitment, and OSS instructional work align across NARA, NPS, and Army institutional histories. The two Oregon institutional references remain separate pending better chronology.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 20, University of Oregon records, and Oregon State athletic records to resolve the institutional sequence and confirm the exact Military Police-to-OSS transfer date.
